advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the parity guard to assert every name in vote.needs is a defined job in gerrit-verify.yaml (and, ideally, that gating reusables receive the Gerrit patchset inputs), not just a name-superset.
evidence: `missing_gating_jobs` computes `required - vote_needs(gerrit_workflow)` — it only checks names are present in needs, never that gerrit_workflow['jobs'] defines them or that they pass gerrit-refspec (scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:104-107)

The error text tells maintainers to 'ensure the job actually runs in that lane (call the shared reusable with the Gerrit patchset inputs...)' but nothing in the script validates that (scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:123-125)

Ticket rationale: 'Nothing structurally forbade the drift' (commit message / docstring lines 14-15) — a name-only superset check still permits a needs entry that is undefined or checks out branch-head.
advisory.finding: The parity guard only checks that vote.needs is a name-superset of source-lane job names; it never verifies each name in vote.needs corresponds to a DEFINED job in gerrit-verify.yaml that actually runs on the patchset. A vote.needs entry with no backing job (or a job that checks out branch-head instead of the Gerrit refspec) passes the guard, so the 'structurally forbid drift' guarantee the ticket targets is only partially delivered.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either make the guard actually inspect job `if:` conditions, or correct the docstring/test language to state it treats all non-EXCLUDED jobs as required (not 'unconditional').
evidence: `gating_job_names` returns `{name for name in jobs if name not in excluded}` — no inspection of a job's `if:` condition (scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:82-85)

Docstring claims it fails 'unless vote.needs is a superset of every unconditional gating job' (scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:16-17) and test docstrings say 'unconditional jobs that gate main' (tests/unit/test_verify_gate_parity.py:5-6)
`prompt-eval.yml`'s required `eval-discipline` job actually carries `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'` (prompt-eval.yml:45), showing 'unconditional' is not the real criterion the guard applies.
advisory.finding: The docstring and tests describe the guard as enforcing 'unconditional gating jobs', but `gating_job_names` treats EVERY non-excluded job as required regardless of its `if:` condition. The guard cannot distinguish an unconditional job from a conditional (off-critical-path) one; it relies solely on the hand-maintained EXCLUDED_JOBS, so a newly-added conditional job in a source lane will be falsely demanded in vote.needs until manually excluded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test exercising a source-lane job that carries an `if:` condition (both a required one like eval-discipline and an excluded conditional one) so the checker's gating-classification behavior around conditional jobs is pinned.
evidence: scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:82 `def gating_job_names(workflow: dict, ...)` returns `{name for name in jobs if name not in excluded}` — no inspection of `if:`
tests/unit/test_verify_gate_parity.py:45 `_source` builds `{name: {"runs-on": "ubuntu-latest"} ...}` — never sets an `if:` condition
prompt-eval.yml:45 `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' }}` on the REQUIRED eval-discipline job, and eval-live/external are conditional jobs relying on EXCLUDED_JOBS
ABSENCE: no test asserts that a conditional job absent from EXCLUDED_JOBS is (or is not) reported by missing_gating_jobs, nor that eval-discipline's `if:` does not remove it from the required set
advisory.finding: The parity checker classifies a job as 'gating' purely by presence in a source-lane's jobs map minus EXCLUDED_JOBS (gating_job_names ignores any `if:` condition), so conditional non-critical-path jobs (external, eval-live) are handled only via a hand-maintained exclude list. No test exercises a source workflow containing an `if:`-guarded job, so the guard's behavior for a future conditional job forgotten from EXCLUDED_JOBS — and its correct counting of the required-but-conditional eval-discipline (which carries `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`) — is unverified. The synthetic _source() helper never emits an `if:` key.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use capsys in the drift test to assert evaluate() prints the `::error::` line and the sorted MISSING-jobs list.
evidence: tests/unit/test_verify_gate_parity.py:66 `assert rc != 0` — only the exit code is checked
scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py:122 prints the `MISSING from vote.needs ... {sorted(missing)}` diagnostic that no test captures
advisory.finding: test_guard_main_exit_nonzero_on_drift declares `monkeypatch` and `capsys` fixtures but uses neither, and asserts only the return code; the operator-facing drift diagnostic (`::error::` line and the `MISSING from vote.needs: [...]` list printed by evaluate()) is never asserted in any test.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_guard_main_exit_nonzero_on_drift, capture `out = capsys.readouterr().out` and assert `"eval-discipline" in out` and `"::error::" in out`; drop the unused monkeypatch fixture.
